clue.text: It contains ale, brewed for disciplinary use

indicators.note: ale that is brewed is worked up from its ingredients, so these words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a drink contains ale brewed for a disciplinary purpose, as if beer were a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' shuffles all thirteen letters of IT CONTAINS ALE; the surface makes 'brewed' describe the ale.
explanation.definitionFit: The cat-o'-nine-tails was a knotted whip once used to flog sailors and prisoners as punishment.

clue.text: Game of catch — first to get caught by 24

parts.note: to catch an illness is to contract it

indicators.note: the letter is held inside the other word, caught by it

parts.note: the answer to 24 down, a newly married woman

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A game of catch in which the first player to get the ball is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught by' puts G, from 'first to get', inside BRIDE (the answer to 24 down) to make BRIDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Contract bridge is the card game in which partnerships bid to make a contracted number of tricks.

definitions.note: the definition describes creatures by where they live, in Lewis Carroll's nonsense poem

indicators.note: a spoilt ballot paper is spoiled, so the letters of the word are messed up

explanation.surface: Ballot papers were spoiled somewhere strange, in a nonsense landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: Carroll's Jabberwocky has 'the slithy toves did gyre and gimble in the wabe'; the definition identifies the creatures by that line.
explanation.definitionFit: Toves are Lewis Carroll's invented creatures that gyre and gimble in the wabe in Jabberwocky.

parts.note: a nut is a biscuit, as in ginger nut, and a cracker is a savoury biscuit
a nut is a biscuit, as in ginger nut, and a cracker is a savoury biscuit

explanation.surface: Two biscuits arrive in a bathroom attached to a hotel bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'en suite' is not bathroom fittings: it points to Tchaikovsky's Nutcracker Suite.
explanation.definitionFit: Tchaikovsky's ballet music is best known as the Nutcracker Suite, so it comes in a suite.

indicators.note: the word are goes inside the retreat

parts.note: a nest is a snug retreat or hideaway

explanation.surface: Those pulling back are the closest.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearest means the closest, at the smallest distance away.

clue.text: Proposition from Merioneth not in order

indicators.note: the letters of the word in are not to be included when the place name is rearranged
the remaining letters of the Welsh county are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A statement taken from the Welsh county is disorganised.
explanation.walkthrough: Merioneth is an old Welsh county. 'not in' removes I and N from its letters; 'order' rearranges the remaining MEROETH.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a theorem is a proposition to be proved.

indicators.note: the top letter, the first one in a down clue, is removed

parts.note: an aisle is a passage between rows of seats

explanation.surface: A corridor, and an instruction to trim an inch off the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inch' is not the measure but the Scottish word for a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland an inch is a small island, as in Inchcolm.

clue.text: Fastidious Miss West turns up surrounded by marmalade

indicators.note: the reversed name sits inside the slang word

parts.note: squish is old schoolboy slang for marmalade

indicators.note: in a down clue the name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Mae West was the Hollywood actress

explanation.surface: A fussy Mae West arrives, smothered in marmalade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses MAE to EAM, and 'surrounded by' puts it inside SQUISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeamish can mean overscrupulous or fussy, easily put off, hence fastidious.

clue.text: Coin-operated? Then I only spent change

indicators.note: the letters of these words are changed into another order, with a nod to loose coins

explanation.surface: A vending machine sees the speaker spend only loose coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' looks like the coins but rearranges THEN I ONLY SPENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A penny-in-the-slot machine is one worked by dropping a coin in it.

parts.note: NO is the standard abbreviation for number, as in No 10
to vitiate a contract is to make it void, to invalidate it

explanation.surface: A figure that would undo someone's period of trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A novitiate is the trial period a novice spends before taking vows, a probation.

clue.text: Being worthy of contempt, I deserted girl

indicators.note: the letter I has deserted, gone missing from, the girl's name

parts.note: Louise is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A jilted speaker admits that a girl left him because he was contemptible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a noun here, a creature, not the verb; the clue's comma pretends otherwise.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse, besides the insect, is a contemptible person, a creature deserving scorn.

clue.text: One leaving bed and in flight

definitions.meaning: someone who gets up in the morning
one of the steps in a flight of stairs, specifically the upright part of each step

explanation.definitionFit: An early riser gets up from bed; in a staircase the riser is the vertical board of each step.

definitions.meaning: an old legal term for the circuit travelled by itinerant judges
the surname given to Jane in Charlotte Bronte's novel

explanation.definitionFit: Historically an eyre was a judges' travelling circuit court; Jane Eyre is the Bronte heroine.

definitions.meaning: to pop something is slang for pledging it at a pawnbroker's
a piece in chess is often called a man

explanation.definitionFit: To pawn a watch is to pop it at the pawnshop; a pawn is the humblest chessman.

parts.note: players of lawn bowls on a green that rises to a hump in the middle, not flat

explanation.definitionFit: A crown green is a bowling green raised in the centre, used for a northern English form of bowls.

annotationWithheld.why: Mimic with (or without) I Ac (4-3): 'Mimic' defines COPYCAT, but no reading of 'with (or without) I Ac' builds the letters; the italic device is not explained and no blog or database gives it.

clue.text: "The King's Head" — no shelter in there

definitions.note: read as the king has: the definition is the king, with 's as a link

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the word for head

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
O is nought, nothing
a tent is a shelter

explanation.surface: A pub called the King's Head offers no shelter inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The pub name misleads; 'The King' is the definition with 's as 'has', and 'in there' puts O and TENT inside PATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A potentate is a monarch or ruler with great power.

clue.text: Gun gets the bird with one

parts.note: a martin is a bird of the swallow family
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A shooter bags a bird with a single shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Martini-Henry was a Victorian British army rifle; the drink is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Martini-Henry rifle, often just called a Martini, was a standard British service firearm.

definitions.meaning: in law an attack on a person
a set of artillery pieces grouped together

explanation.definitionFit: Battery is the legal term for physical attack; an artillery battery is a unit of cannon.

parts.note: everyone ages, so no one becomes less old over time

explanation.definitionFit: No person grows more youthful; everyone ages.

clue.text: Part of ship gets dangerous in reach of missile

parts.note: the bows are the front part of a ship
hot can mean dangerous, as in a situation too hot to handle

explanation.surface: The front of a vessel comes under fire within range of a missile.
explanation.walkthrough: The split falls after BOWS, not after BOW; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowshot is the distance an arrow can be shot from a bow, its range.

clue.text: Gun makes animal cry; many animals and king intervene

indicators.note: the animals and king come between the letters of the cry

parts.note: baa is the cry of a sheep
a zoo houses many animals
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A gun makes a creature yelp as a herd and a king step in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intervene' puts ZOO and K between BA and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazooka is a portable anti-tank rocket launcher, a kind of gun.

definitions.note: the clue points to the answer of 6 down, a small island

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Mechanical: one thing placed on another.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' stands for the answer to 6 down; Iona is a small island in the Scottish Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small Hebridean island, famous for St Columba's monastery.

definitions.meaning: fine soft fluff, like the down on a peach

explanation.definitionFit: Fuzz is soft fluffy down, and in slang it is the cops.

parts.note: to gab is to chatter idly
le is French for the, a foreign word for it

explanation.surface: Someone talks to an overseas celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Clark Gable was the Hollywood star of Gone with the Wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark Gable was a leading Hollywood actor of the 1930s and 1940s.

clue.text: You can't miss her any more

definitions.text: You can't miss her any more

parts.words: You can't miss her any more
parts.note: a woman who has just married can no longer be addressed as Miss

explanation.definitionFit: A newly married woman takes the title Mrs, no longer Miss.

definitions.meaning: slang for corrupt or dishonest, as in a crooked copper

explanation.definitionFit: A dishonest policeman is called bent; a bent is also a natural inclination.

clue.text: "A fine and private place" of some importance

definitions.meaning: a quotation from Marvell's poem To His Coy Mistress, describing the tomb
weighty, serious, as in a serious matter

explanation.definitionFit: Marvell wrote of the tomb that it is a fine and private place; a serious matter is weighty.

parts.note: a goose is a tailor's smoothing iron, named for its goose-neck handle
a maiden is a young girl

explanation.surface: A medieval torture device, the iron maiden, is wryly called a birdwatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The iron maiden' looks like the torture cabinet; it splits into the tailor's iron and a maiden. The definition is cryptic: she watches over birds as a herder.
explanation.definitionFit: A goose girl tends a flock of geese, so she literally watches birds; the question mark flags the pun.

clue.text: In hospitality tent, men retain wild characters

indicators.note: the letters of these words are let loose, running wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Inside a corporate hospitality marquee, men hold on to unruly guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild characters' tells you to shuffle TENT MEN RETAIN; 'In' is a link that suits the marquee picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment of guests, with food and drink, is what hospitality means.
